learningObjectives: Recognize automation spanning UI, documents, data and services.
Identify the technology areas covered by these independent notes.
Check version-specific prerequisites and workspace contents.
Distinguish practice material from official course and certification requirements.

elements.description: A business process can span a web form, email, a document, a workbook, a Windows application and a mobile screen. These independent notes examine the Tosca technologies used for such steps.
TBox provides a shared model for Engines 3.0. Modules and TestSteps provide familiar building blocks; supported controls, ActionModes and prerequisites still depend on the selected technology.

elements.text: The signed-in AE1 course describes training developed with Tosca 16.0. Its overview covers framework, Excel, PDF, mail, Windows, self-healing, file/folder operations, custom/image controls and mobile, with Vision AI marked optional. The local notes supplement this course with versioned public documentation.

bulletPoints: Use the engine and control capabilities appropriate to each part of the process.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: What you will be able to do

elements.title: Verified course topics and local study outline
items: Framework — explore the concept of TBox automation frameworks.
Excel — steer and test Excel workbooks and the Excel application, verify cell special properties, compare workbooks, and steer Excel macros.
PDF — scan and test PDF files, create and manage Anchors in the PDF Scan, and compare PDF files using Standard Modules.
Mail — send and receive mails using the Tosca Mail Engine.
Windows desktop — steer and test applications using the UIA and WinX Engines.
Resilience — use the Self-healing property of Tosca.
Files — use Standard Modules to automate file and folder operations.
Hard-to-identify controls — create image-based controls, and install and use Custom controls.
Mobile — create Mobile TestCases using the Tricentis Mobile Agent and Mobile Engine.
Vision AI — inspect its documented setup and supported controls.

bulletPoints: Notice the pattern: most lessons are 'here is a technology, here is the Engine that reaches it'. Two lessons (Self-healing, Custom/Image controls) are instead about what to do when identification itself is the problem.

elements.title: Prerequisites
items: The Academy lists AS1 and AS2 prior training and access to a licensed Tosca installation.
Use a supported Tosca installation and valid entitlement; inspect current system requirements.
Check dependencies for the selected engine, such as the target application, source files, mail connection or mobile agent.
Use approved test accounts and data in a test environment.

elements.text: The original course was developed with Tosca 16.0. Version differences can include functionality and deprecations, not only screenshots; consult the matching manual and upgrade changes rather than assuming every old example remains compatible.

bulletPoints: Unlike AS1/AS2, several AE1 lessons depend on software outside Tosca (Excel, a mail server, a mobile device). Check you have these before starting the relevant lesson.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Exercise prerequisite: create the AE1 workspace

elements.description: The original download package contains both base and solution TSU subsets. Their object structures were read without importing or executing them. Use the base for exercises and the solution for comparison in an isolated training workspace; inspect the actual imported Modules/TestCases and version compatibility.

elements.title: Prepare the workspace
items: Obtain the official base and solution subsets from the course downloads; inspect the version and contents.
Create the workspace using the documented workflow for your installed version.
Inspect the Modules and TestCases actually imported before using them.

elements.text: The 2026.1 manual places technology modules under Standard modules → Engines. Older subsets can use different folder names; navigate the actual imported tree.

The source notes that an imported subset may not be immediately visible: search under Section and open it. Reading the provided solution or its stored logs does not count as a new execution of the tests.

bulletPoints: Folder names and available Modules depend on the supplied subset/version.

elements.description: The original welcome recommends video lessons, associated practice exercises and solution review. It describes eleven lessons including two theory lessons, with Hands-on guides and Vision AI Theory optional. The welcome states that the course Final Exam excludes those optional sections. This is the declaration for this Academy course, not a general rule for other certifications.

elements.text: The course welcome requires lesson training elements, including exercises, notes and knowledge checks, to be completed before the Final Exam is accessible. A local Quilyn quiz score is independent practice feedback and does not unlock the Academy exam or issue its certificate.

bulletPoints: Use the course’s current completion controls; do not infer official exam progress from local practice.
The original welcome excludes its optional Hands-on/Vision AI sections from its Final Exam.

examPitfalls.title: Skipping practical validation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reading a workflow does not prove its integration works.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Run a controlled example and inspect assertions and dependencies.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming examination requirements
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An independent note cannot establish which official sections are optional or examinable.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the original welcome’s course-specific rules: optional Hands-on/Vision AI material is excluded from this Final Exam, and course training elements gate its access. Local practice does not satisfy those course controls.

examPitfalls.title: Treating upgrades as cosmetic
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A newer build can change behavior and remove features.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Read version-matched requirements and upgrade changes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What distinguishes AE1 from the Automation Specialist (AS1/AS2) courses?

options.text: AE1 replaces the TestCase/Module workflow with a scripting language.
AE1 extends automation beyond web applications to Excel, PDF, mail, Windows desktop, mobile, and file operations.
AE1 is about test design rather than automation.

practiceQuiz.hint: The course title is 'Automating beyond web applications'.
practiceQuiz.rationale: These notes cover non-web technologies alongside browser automation. Tosca uses Modules and TestSteps across engines; technology prerequisites and supported operations still vary.

optionExplanations.A: Modules/TestSteps remain the model; a scripting replacement is not the stated purpose.
optionExplanations.B: The topics span these non-web technologies.
optionExplanations.C: Performance testing is not the scope described.
optionExplanations.D: The notes concern executable automation, not only data design.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before attempting a lesson that uses an additional technology, what should a learner check?

options.text: Only whether the lesson video played to the end
The engine requirements, supported version and actual workspace Modules
Only whether a Final Exam button is visible
Nothing; every technology needs no external setup

practiceQuiz.hint: A common framework does not remove technology dependencies.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Check the engine requirements and actual workspace contents. Video completion, a guessed folder path or a general Tosca installation alone does not establish that a specific example can run.

optionExplanations.A: Watching a video does not validate dependencies.
optionExplanations.B: These checks establish the prerequisites for the selected technology.
optionExplanations.C: Exam UI does not validate the technical setup.
optionExplanations.D: Individual technologies can require additional setup.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How should a learner handle a newer Tosca version than the version used by an example?

options.text: Require every dialog to match the recording pixel for pixel
Consult version-matched requirements and documented functionality changes
Delete all existing tests without reviewing compatibility

practiceQuiz.hint: Upgrade changes can affect behavior, not only appearance.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use matching requirements and upgrade documentation. Pixel matching, assuming identical behavior or deleting tests is not a substitute for reviewing changes.

optionExplanations.A: Dialog appearance is not a compatibility test.
optionExplanations.B: Version-matched documentation identifies relevant functional changes.
optionExplanations.C: Upgrades can change functionality or deprecate features.
